leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members name optical lattice clocks (Katori and Ye) as their preferred single-part configuration. They share the two-person credit (Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice idea, Ye for record accuracy and many-body clock work), the 10^-18 performance, and independent reproduction across laboratories. They do not share one citation wording: some say 'time and frequency measurement', others 'atomic timekeeping' or 'frequency measurement'. All five themselves flag the same reservations: overlap with the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, the unfinished redefinition of the second, and omitted clock groups. Olsson moved to B024 from B001 after reading the opening ballots, and Kroll and Lindroth disclose field proximity or a Boulder research stay linked to the comb prize. Their lists of alternatives (B003, B014, B023, B001) differ.

Two members name magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero, Bistritzer) as their preferred configuration, on the strength of the 2011 prediction followed by the 2018 discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and a large independent follow-on field. Their citations are similar but not identical. Both concede that the superconducting mechanism is unsettled and that the three-name limit leaves out the first experimental author and other early groups. Eriksson says B024 would be an acceptable choice if the moire interpretation is judged too immature, and Danielsson calls B024 the safe and defensible alternative. B003 is named as an alternative by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, so it has wider second-choice support than first-choice support.

One member prefers active matter and flocking (Toner, Ramaswamy, Vicsek) as a new conceptual class of nonequilibrium statistical physics. He states that no other member put B006 in a preferred configuration, that quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents is weak, and that B024 is the stronger candidate if sharp measurable outcomes are the test. He lists B003 and B024 as alternatives. The three-name cutoff against Marchetti, Cates, Simha and Chate is an open question.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members propose the same two names (Katori and Ye) for B024 in their opening ballots, and in round 1 every member lists B024 or B003 as either a preferred configuration or an alternative (Mehlig lists both as alternatives).

Members who prefer B024 and members who prefer B003 each acknowledge the other candidate as a serious option rather than dismissing it; Danielsson and Eriksson say they could accept B024, and Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce all list B003 as their first alternative.

The 10^-18 performance, cross-laboratory reproduction and the compact Katori-Ye attribution of B024 are not contested by any member; the disputes concern novelty relative to earlier prizes and timing, not the quality of the result.

Members agree that the pairing mechanism of superconductivity in twisted graphene is unresolved and that any B003 citation must be built on flat bands and correlated states and avoid claims about pairing.
No member advocates B043 (circuit QED), citing the 2025 circuit prize, and Johansson states he will not advocate it because of his Chalmers and WACQT ties.
Several members note that B058 and B001 each have only one first-place preferrer and no visible majority path (Eriksson says so of B058, and Olsson of B001).
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus invention: Danielsson, Eriksson and Pearce set B003 (new state of matter) against B024 (refined measurement). Pearce says B003 and B023 carry a stronger claim to opening a new field. B024 supporters answer that the many-atom magic-wavelength scheme is a distinct regime from the comb and single-ion control.

Whether metrology is a physics discovery for this prize: Pearce flags that a clock prize may be seen as an instrument achievement, while Kroll, Lindroth and Johansson argue the physics result is decisive and quantitative.

Whether the topological insulator proposal (B023) justifies a second topology prize after 2016: Mehlig is recorded by Danielsson as the source of the overlap concern, Eriksson calls it the best fallback if B003 stalls, and Pearce lists it as his second alternative.

Whether a methodological tool such as Car-Parrinello (B058) counts as a discovery: Eriksson supports it as an alternative, while Danielsson and Mehlig doubt it, as chemistry or as a method built on already honoured density-functional theory.
Whether the Toner-Tu theory in B006 has enough quantitative confirmation, with Mehlig himself calling the exponents only partly confirmed.
attribution_disputes: B024: omitted clock contributors (Lemonde, Sterr, Hollberg, Ludlow, Hinkley, the SYRTE, PTB and NIST groups and the ion-clock leaders) are cited by Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce as a possible claim against a two-name prize, and Olsson asks whether Ye's role is co-invention or realization.

B003: the three-name credit omits the first experimental author (Yuan Cao) and other early groups (Dean, Young, Yazdani, Kim). Eriksson also cites earlier twist-angle work (Lopes dos Santos). Olsson would credit only MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero according to Eriksson's response, and Eriksson would keep Bistritzer as first author of the 2011 calculation.
B006: three names against the wider field (Marchetti, Cates, Simha, Chate), per Mehlig.
B014 and B035 member-level credit differences recorded in the opening rankings are not argued in round 1 and should not be assumed settled.
maturity_disputes: B003: Kroll, Johansson and Eriksson raise the risk that recognition is early because the superconducting mechanism and some correlated phases are still debated, while Danielsson cites high-temperature superconductors as precedent for rewarding the observation before the mechanism. The members differ on how much interpretive maturity is required.

B024: Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce regard the physics as mature but note a fair objection that the SI second has not yet been redefined; Lindroth calls this objection weak and Pearce says an unfavourable reading would treat the redefinition as the formal consummation. Whether to wait is unresolved.
B006: the order of the Vicsek transition was disputed for years, and quantitative tests of Toner-Tu scaling remain incomplete.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson-Goran: professor at Chalmers and director of WACQT, with documented Chalmers colleagues and ties to the 2025 circuit prize; discloses a specific recusal issue for B043 and states he will not advocate it. He reports no apparent conflict for B024, B003 or B014.

Kroll-Stefan: spent a doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, whose frequency-comb prize forms part of the B024 boundary argument; also works in laser spectroscopy and has taken part in WACQT. He asks whether the Hall connection requires recusal on the clock discussion.
Lindroth-Eva: documented collaborations with L'Huillier, the Lund attosecond group and Keller's group; no documented tie to Katori or Ye, but she notes field adjacency to atomic physics.

Olsson-Eva: long-running exchanges with Japanese universities including a University of Tokyo fellowship, with one B024 name based in Japan, no documented relationship; also a professional user of aberration-corrected TEM, relevant to B001.
Mehlig-Bernhard: field proximity to active matter (B006) with no documented tie to Toner, Ramaswamy or Vicsek.
Pearce-Mark (chair): no conflict apparent for B024; same broad field as B035 (IceCube), which I ranked third and did not include in my preferred configuration, flagged as potential bias.
Danielsson-Ulf and Eriksson-Olle: no specific conflict recorded; Eriksson notes a possible bias as a computational materials theorist regarding B058.
questions_for_round2: Does the committee treat optical lattice clocks (B024) as distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 single-ion prizes, and if so what wording in the citation would state that distinction?
Should the pending redefinition of the SI second be treated as a prerequisite for recognizing B024, or is it irrelevant to the discovery?
What degree of interpretive maturity must B003 meet, given the unresolved superconducting mechanism, and can members state what evidence would change their view?
Should a B003 prize be two names (MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero) or three (adding Bistritzer), and how does the committee justify omitting Yuan Cao and the early confirming groups?
Is the Katori-Ye credit for B024 secure against the claims of Lemonde, Sterr, Hollberg, Ludlow, Hinkley and the ion-clock groups, and is Ye credited for co-invention or for realization?
Do the Kroll (Hall laboratory stay) and Olsson (Japanese university ties) disclosures require any recusal or other handling on B024, and does the committee want a formal ruling?
If the committee weighs discovery against metrology, which of B024 or B003 does it prefer, and would the other be acceptable as the final choice for those who ranked it first?
Do B023, B014 and B058 remain live alternatives for round 2, or does the committee narrow to B024, B003 and B006?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows a committee centred on two candidates: B024 is the preferred configuration of five members and B003 of two, with one member preferring B006. Both camps list the other as an alternative and state their own reservations, which are mostly about novelty relative to earlier prizes, the redefinition of the second, interpretive maturity, and credit at the edges. The count reflects only the positions written in the eight files; the committee has not yet tested the novelty, maturity and credit arguments in discussion.
